fatal_errors: The proposed humid oxidative annealing intervention is unrelated to the target intervention: a closed-loop, high-throughput synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning, and Bayesian-optimisation campaign.
The asserted conversion of the starting alloy into a nanoporous high-entropy oxide that stabilizes sub-nanometric PGM sites is not established by the cited evidence.
The cited studies do not demonstrate the claimed combined performance against hydrocarbons, NO and water below 150 °C after vehicle-relevant severe ageing.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad activity–poisoning–durability problem and supplies a testable treated-versus-untreated comparison, so it is a scientifically plausible alternative rather than wholly unsupported. However, it does not reconstruct the target discovery strategy, synthesis window, post-ageing design index, or beneficial Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction. Its conditions also differ materially from the target's 900 °C lean/rich water-containing ageing and near-stoichiometric multicomponent feed. The baseline should include aged Pd/Al2O3 and random exploration rather than only an untreated catalyst. E1 supports improved CO oxidation and short-term stability of directly synthesized disordered spinel oxides, while E2 supports hydrothermal stability of Pt deposited on an existing high-entropy oxide at 210 °C. Neither validates forming the proposed porous oxide by annealing the stated alloy, resistance to NO poisoning, hydrocarbon oxidation below 150 °C, or lifetime durability. The experiment is directionally discriminating but lacks a fully specified feed, annealing protocol, hydrocarbon identities, ageing duration, replication, and separate quantitative failure thresholds.
